headline: Growth accelerates, margin expands, buybacks ramp up
summary_short: Mastercard grew Q2 FY2026 net revenue 14% y/y (12% currency-neutral) to $9,277M and diluted EPS 22% y/y to $4.97, as payment-network revenue rose 10% on 8% GDV growth and 12% cross-border volume growth, while value-added services and solutions revenue rose 20%.
summary_long: Net revenue rose 14% y/y (12% currency-neutral) to $9.28B, led by payment-network growth (+10%, on 8% GDV growth, 12% cross-border growth, 9% switched-transactions growth) and value-added services and solutions growth (+20%) in security, digital/authentication and market-insights offerings. Operating margin expanded to 60.2% from 58.7% as expense growth (+10%) trailed revenue growth. Net income rose 19% to $4.39B; diluted EPS rose 22% to $4.97. Cash rose to $11.3B from $9.0B y/y, while long-term debt rose to $22.2B after $5.6B of new debt funded $4.9B of quarterly buybacks and $771M of dividends. No forward guidance was issued in this release.

drivers.explanation: Net revenue grew 14% (12% currency-neutral) on growth in payment network revenue (+10%, or +8% currency-neutral, driven by 8% GDV growth, 12% cross-border volume growth and 9% switched-transactions growth) and value-added services and solutions revenue (+20%, or +18% currency-neutral) from security, digital/authentication, consumer-engagement and market-insights offerings.
Diluted EPS rose 22%, tracking the 19% net income increase plus a 2.9% lower diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.
Tracks the diluted-EPS move; basic EPS rose 22% on a similarly lower basic weighted-average share count (882M vs 908M a year ago).

Net income rose 19% on 17% higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate (20.0% vs 20.8%) reflecting partially offsetting tax impacts including discrete tax benefits, partly offset by higher income tax expense in dollar terms.
Rose 17% (14% currency-neutral) as operating expenses grew only 10% (primarily on higher general and administrative expenses) versus 14% revenue growth; operating margin expanded to 60.2% from 58.7%.
A Yahoo-derived figure Mastercard doesn't disclose as a line item; the +16.7% y/y increase roughly tracks the 14% revenue growth given only 10% expense growth.
A Yahoo-derived figure tracking the 17% operating-income increase described above.
A Yahoo-derived figure adding depreciation and amortization ($309M, +10% y/y) back to EBIT; tracks the operating-profit increase.
Tracks the 17% operating-income increase; other income (expense) was favorable by $4M y/y, roughly flat, on lower equity-investment losses partly offsetting higher interest expense.

Cash and cash equivalents rose to $11.3B from $9.0B a year ago; per the six-month cash-flow statement, $5.6B of net new debt proceeds and $6.8B of operating cash flow outpaced $8.9B of treasury-stock purchases and $1.5B of dividends paid.

Increase to $22.2B from $19.0B is consistent with $5.6B of new debt proceeds, net of discounts, reported in the six-month financing-activities cash flow; the release does not separately narrate the debt raise.
Rose to $2.46B from $1.75B q/q, consistent with a portion of long-term debt becoming current; the release does not separately explain the reclassification.

Fell to $5.61B from $7.85B a year ago as $8.9B of H1 treasury-stock purchases and $1.5B of dividends paid outpaced $8.27B of H1 net income added to retained earnings; not separately explained in the release.
Diluted share count fell 2.9% y/y to 883M, consistent with the company's disclosed buyback activity, including 9.8 million shares repurchased in Q2 alone at a cost of $4.9 billion.

CEO Michael Miebach said results were "above expectations" with 14% y/y net revenue growth, citing new partnerships in Mexico and the UAE and a market-first Agentic Payment capability as expanding commerce opportunities.
